title: Strawberry Jam-Filled Orange Doughnuts
summary: Soft orange-scented doughnuts enriched with olive oil and soured cream, filled with strawberry jam.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook (or large bowl)
baking trays lined with lightly floured baking paper
piping bag with a 6 mm plain nozzle
large heavy pan or casserole, at least 24 cm wide
wire rack over a tray lined with kitchen paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Whisk the flour, sugar, yeast, salt and orange zest in the mixer bowl. In a jug whisk the water, soured cream, olive oil, egg and vanilla, pour them in and knead on medium-low for about 8 min until the dough is smooth and soft.

steps.title: First rise
steps.text: Cover and leave in a warm spot for 1-1.5 h, until doubled.

steps.title: Cut the rounds
steps.text: Knock back the dough, pat it out 1.5 cm thick on a floured surface and stamp out 6 cm rounds. Press the scraps together once and cut again to get 14. Place them on the lined trays.

steps.title: Prove
steps.text: Cover loosely and leave for 30-40 min until puffy and light.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into the wide pan until it is roughly 4 cm deep (half full at most) and bring it up to 170 °C on the thermometer.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Fry 4 at a time for 1.5-2 min a side at 165-170 °C, until deep golden with a pale ring around the middle; a probe in the centre should read about 90 °C. Drain on the rack and let them cool for 15 min.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Push the chopstick down through the top of each doughnut to the centre and wiggle it to open a pocket. Pipe in about 20 g of jam, drawing the nozzle out slowly so a little dome of jam sits on top.

tips: The most common mistake is frying too hot; the small rounds brown in seconds and stay raw inside, so keep to 165-170 °C.
Let them cool before filling or the jam will run out.
Smooth, seedless jam pipes much more easily than chunky jam.
Raspberry or cherry jam works just as well.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Best on the day. Keep for up to 1 day in an airtight container at room temperature.
